caseStudies.name: Hospital Operations Platform
caseStudies.tagline: Billing, prescriptions, wards, lab and a two-tier pharmacy for a multi-specialty hospital, all in one system.
caseStudies.oneLiner: A web platform with a companion Android staff app that runs a multi-specialty hospital day to day: patient registration and billing, digital prescriptions, in-patient admissions, the pathology lab, and a complete pharmacy from vendor purchasing to the counter sale.
caseStudies.role: Sole developer: architecture, backend, frontend, mobile and deployment
caseStudies.confidentialNote: This is an internal system built under a confidentiality agreement, so it has no public link and the client is not named. Screenshots with anonymized data are coming soon.
problem: A multi-specialty hospital runs several businesses under one roof: OPD consultations, in-patient wards, a pathology lab, a pharmacy counter, a hospital pharmacy and a central medicine store that supplies them. Each has its own staff, billing and stock, and they all touch the same patients and the same medicines.

Without one system, bills, prescriptions and lab reports live in separate places, pharmacy stock drifts away from what is on the shelf with no trail of who moved what, vendor reordering is manual, and near-expiry stock is noticed too late.
The platform gives every department its own role-based workspace on shared data, and gives the owner and admin analytics, audit trails and security controls over all of it.

roles.name: Admin
roles.does: Every module, users and roles, security, automations, request logs, audit trails, exports

roles.name: Owner
roles.does: Business analytics, pharmacy accounts, expenses, approvals for returns and stock-sensitive operations

roles.name: Front desk
roles.does: Patient registration, OPD invoices, express billing, lab reports, IPD

roles.name: Pharmacy counter
roles.does: Pharmacy billing, stock requests to the store, expiring-stock list

roles.name: Central store
roles.does: Purchase invoices, vendor orders over WhatsApp, returns, payment dues

roles.name: Nurse
roles.does: Patients, billing, IPD, digitizing doctors' prescriptions

roles.name: Doctor
roles.does: Personal analytics and the clinical master lists

roles.name: Pathologist
roles.does: Lab test entry, editing and printing

roles.name: OPD
roles.does: Digitizing prescriptions, also from the mobile app

features.title: Pharmacy: counter, hospital pharmacy and central store
items: Counter billing with batch allocation: earliest expiry first, strips and loose tablets, near-expiry batches never sold, discounts guarded by margin
Store-to-counter stock requests with approval, batch allocation and a receipt check against the system count
Purchase invoices that go through review, then enter stock with GST, discounts and free-offer quantities
Auto-suggested vendor orders from stock limits, sent to vendors over WhatsApp
Customer returns, pull-backs to the store, vendor return notes and credit notes
Expiring, slow-moving and stale stock reports, margin and selling-ratio analysis

features.title: Stock ledger: a passbook for every medicine
items: Every sale, return, receipt and correction writes an immutable ledger entry: before, after, batch-wise change, who did it and which bill caused it
A printable statement per medicine and date range with opening balance, running balance and closing balance
Any stock change made outside the ledger is flagged on the statement

features.title: Digital prescriptions
items: Handwritten prescriptions transcribed into structured complaints, diagnoses, investigations, medicines and advice
Suggestions ranked by what that doctor has used before, then by what other doctors used
Curated clinical master lists with an approval flow and synonyms
Prescription lines are marked as billed automatically, so billing staff see what is still pending

features.title: Patients, OPD, IPD and lab
items: Patient registration and advanced search, OPD invoices with print-ready formats
Express billing for quick counter sales, converted into full invoices later
Admissions, wards and beds, outstanding-payment tracking; pharmacy sales for insured patients are added to their admission automatically
Lab test catalogue, result entry and printable reports

features.title: Security and administration
items: Brute-force lockout per account and per IP, revocable server-side sessions, active-session and login history
Two-step login for the web, with a rotating 6-digit code shown on the staff member's registered phone
Mobile devices must be approved by an admin; refresh tokens rotate on every use
Admin-scheduled automations with run logs, plus an operations console with health, request analytics and error logs

engineering.title: All-or-nothing stock movements
engineering.body: A pharmacy bill touches the invoice, several stock documents, the patient's admission and the prescription markers. These used to be sequential writes, so a failure halfway, or two counters billing the same medicine at once, could deduct stock without creating a bill. I moved every critical flow onto MongoDB multi-document transactions on a replica set. Write conflicts re-run on fresh stock, and an idempotency key turns double-clicks into "invoice already created". Each flow was verified with scripted failure and concurrency tests.

engineering.title: A ledger that cannot drift
engineering.body: Every stock movement becomes one small, immutable document written in the same transaction as the stock change. Each entry stores the balance after it, so a statement for any date range reads only that range, with keyset pagination and indexes matched to the real queries. In a test with 3,000 entries for one medicine, a 10-day slice from the middle came back in single-digit milliseconds.

engineering.title: Authentication for shared hospital terminals
engineering.body: JWTs are backed by Redis sessions, so any session can be revoked. Staff with several roles switch the active role inside one session. Web logins can require a TOTP code (RFC 6238, secrets encrypted with AES-256-GCM) shown on the staff member's phone. The mobile app uses short-lived access tokens and rotating refresh tokens stored only as hashes. If Redis goes down, the system falls back to JWT-only checks instead of locking everyone out.

engineering.title: From monolith to a dedicated API
engineering.body: About 35k lines of Next.js API routes were moved into a standalone Express backend organized by module, with shared middleware for auth, role checks, error handling and responses. The move was tracked with a migration map, so it shipped without breaking the hospital's daily work.

engineering.title: Observability without extra infrastructure
engineering.body: Every API request goes to hourly JSON-lines logs, kept for 15 days. Failed requests also store their bodies with sensitive fields masked. A request id links ledger entries back to the exact request, and a global Mongoose plugin tracks database queries and cache hits per module.

engineering.title: Background jobs the admin controls
engineering.body: BullMQ workers on Redis run jobs whose schedule the admin edits in the UI. Jobs retry with exponential backoff and keep run logs. One of them recalculates minimum and maximum stock for each medicine from sales history, which then feeds the auto-suggested vendor orders.

architecture.label: Backend
items: Express REST API behind a reverse proxy
Stock ledger, audit trails, request logs

architecture.label: Data & services
items: Server disk: uploads, APK releases, logs

caseStudies.name: FlashVouchers
caseStudies.tagline: A multi-country coupon platform with a website, a Chrome extension, an admin CMS and an MCP server for AI assistants.
caseStudies.oneLiner: A coupon and deals platform that helps shoppers in several countries find verified discount codes. It ships as a public website, a Chrome extension and an upcoming mobile app, and the team runs it all from one admin panel that ChatGPT or Claude can connect to.
caseStudies.role: Sole developer: website, admin panel, API, extension and mobile app
problem: Shoppers waste time hunting for coupon codes that are expired, fake or not valid in their country.

Coupon publishers have the opposite problem. They have to turn a constant stream of offers from affiliate networks into country-specific, SEO-friendly pages, keep those pages fresh, and earn commission on every click.

FlashVouchers serves both sides: a fast storefront and browser extension for shoppers, and a CMS for the publisher's team built around merchants, offers and affiliate networks, with per-country content in each country's own language and AI assistants that can do the data entry.

roles.name: Visitor
roles.does: Browse stores, categories, offers, events and guides for their country; reveal public codes

roles.name: Member
roles.does: Unlock premium codes, favourite stores, store alerts, revealed-code history, use the extension

roles.name: Admin
roles.does: Every CMS module, roles and security, blog approval, granting MCP write access

roles.name: Content manager
roles.does: Merchant and category content, events, blogs, layouts; read-only MCP access

roles.name: AI client via MCP
roles.does: ChatGPT or Claude acting for a staff member: 23 tools, drafts only, every write audited

features.title: MCP server for the content team
items: Staff connect ChatGPT, Claude or any MCP client to the admin panel with a normal login
Paste an affiliate-network email and the offers are extracted and created as drafts
The assistant writes each country's content in that country's language
Look up and update merchants, offers, categories, blogs and FAQs in plain language

features.title: Multi-country storefront
items: Geo-IP redirect to the visitor's country (India, US, UK, Germany)
Merchants, categories and FAQs carry localized text and SEO fields per country
Offer dates stored in the country's time zone, so a deal expires at local midnight
Store directory, nested category tree, seasonal event pages, blogs and savings guides
JSON-LD structured data across 8 page types

features.title: Reveal-a-code flow and global search
items: Codes are never sent to the browser until the user clicks "Get code"; lists only show the last few characters
Premium codes unlock with sign-in (email, Google or Apple)
Ctrl+K search across stores, offers, categories and blogs, with relevance scoring, highlighted matches and trending suggestions

features.title: Chrome extension
items: Detects a supported store while you shop and shows a small suggestion chip
An in-page panel lists that store's offers; one click reveals, copies and opens the deal
Stays silent on checkout pages and on unsupported sites

features.title: Admin CMS
items: Page builder with 13 content-block types across 5 page contexts, applied as reusable layouts
Affiliate networks with tracking parameters; the final affiliate URL is built automatically
Blog editor (Tiptap) with a draft, review and publish workflow
Cloudinary media gallery, homepage and navbar management, contact inbox
Mobile app content: banners, home sections and stories

engineering.title: A production MCP server with its own OAuth 2.1
engineering.body: The admin app is both the MCP resource and its own OAuth 2.1 authorization server, with dynamic client registration, PKCE, refresh tokens and revocation, so ChatGPT or Claude connect with an ordinary login. Tokens are stored only as SHA-256 hashes. Access is scoped to read or write, only admins can grant write, and write tools are not even registered for read-only sessions.

engineering.title: Making AI writes safe
engineering.body: Everything an AI assistant creates is saved as a draft for human review. Every MCP write is recorded with before and after snapshots, so a bad edit can be reverted, and is attributed as "staff name (via MCP: client)". Rate limits backed by MongoDB work across serverless instances: per token, per write, and per IP for failed authentication.

engineering.title: Protecting the coupon codes
engineering.body: Codes are the business asset. Every public offer response is sanitized to remove the code and affiliate URLs, leaving only a short preview. The code comes back from a dedicated, rate-limited reveal endpoint that checks premium status against the session, and every reveal is logged per offer and per user.

engineering.title: A privacy-first browser extension
engineering.body: The supported-store list is synced in the background and matched locally, so unsupported sites get no script, no network call and no UI. Content scripts are injected on demand, which means new stores work without republishing the extension. The panel lives in a Shadow DOM so it never clashes with the store's CSS.

engineering.title: Localization across 29 languages
engineering.body: Each country has one content language, a currency and its time zones. Merchants, categories, FAQs and blogs keep per-country localizations with their own SEO fields, and the AI assistant is instructed to write in the right language for each country.

engineering.title: Composable page layouts and in-house search
engineering.body: A shared block registry drives both the admin page builder and the public renderer, and data-driven blocks keep pages fresh without manual edits. Search is written in-house with weighted scoring over titles, localized text and SEO keywords, plus debounced, abortable requests and a prefetched suggestion cache.

caseStudies.name: nSplit
caseStudies.tagline: An offline-first group expense splitter for web and Android.
caseStudies.oneLiner: nSplit lets friends, flatmates and travel groups log shared expenses and instantly see who owes whom, on the web or on an Android app that keeps working without internet.
caseStudies.role: Built solo: product design, web, Android, backend and release tooling
problem: When a group shares costs, the money trail gets messy fast: one person pays the hotel, two split a cab, someone covers drinks, and the rent split depends on room size. Groups fall back on chat messages and mental math, which leads to mistakes and awkward conversations.

nSplit gives the group one shared ledger. You log who paid and how to split it, and the app works out everyone's running balance and the fewest payments needed to settle up. It is built for Indian groups first, and it works on a phone with no signal, which is common on trips, syncing once you are back online.

roles.name: Visitor
roles.does: Open a group's share link to see expenses and balances, no account needed

roles.name: Guest app user
roles.does: Use the Android app fully on-device; data is claimed and synced after login

roles.name: Member
roles.does: See everything, suggest expenses and payments for an admin to approve

roles.name: Group admin
roles.does: Manage expenses, members, settings and the share link; approve join requests

features.title: Flexible splitting
items: Split equally, by exact amounts, percentages or shares (a bigger room pays 2 parts)
Amounts calculated in paise with fair rounding
Each expense shows every member's balance before and after

features.title: Smart categories
items: Typing "sabji", "uber to airport" or even a misspelled "grocries" picks the right category and icon
Spending by category: group total or your share, this month, last month or all time

features.title: Offline-first Android app
items: Works fully without internet or an account
Changes are saved on the phone and synced automatically once online
Warns before logout if there are unsynced changes

features.title: Sharing, joining and approvals
items: A read-only share link anyone can open in a browser; it opens straight in the app when installed
Ask to join by picking which group member you are; admins approve or decline
Members' expenses go to a requests inbox for admin approval

features.title: Balances, exports and accounts
items: Who owes whom, simplified settle-up suggestions and one-tap payments
Per-member balance sheet with a running balance
PDF ledger export on web and app with date-range presets
Email or Google sign-in, light and dark themes, in-app feedback

engineering.title: Offline-first sync engine (SQLite to MongoDB)
engineering.body: The app writes every change to SQLite and to an outbox in the same transaction, so nothing is lost if the app is killed. One sync round trip pushes queued changes and pulls everything changed since a saved cursor. Conflicts resolve last-writer-wins, retries are idempotent through a mutation log, and IDs are generated on the device in ObjectId format so a record keeps the same ID everywhere.

engineering.title: One domain package for web and mobile
engineering.body: Split maths, balance simplification, the running ledger, permissions, categories and spending analytics live in one framework-free package with tests. Both the Next.js app and the React Native app use it, so both compute identical balances to the paisa.

engineering.title: Permissions on every write path
engineering.body: Four permission levels map to 17 actions, enforced in the REST API and in the sync endpoint alike, so sync can never remove an account-linked member or the last admin. Approving a request is atomic: it is claimed with a conditional update, so two admins can never apply it twice.

engineering.title: Hinglish- and typo-tolerant categories
engineering.body: Expense titles are normalized and matched against keyword lists that include Hinglish words, plus a phonetic key and one-letter typo matching, with guards so "mouse" is not read as "house". It runs offline on the phone and on the server from the same code.

engineering.title: Google Sign-In and a self-managed release pipeline
engineering.body: Web and Android both get a Google ID token that the server verifies against Google's public keys, and existing email accounts are linked instead of duplicated. Android builds are signed locally through a custom Expo config plugin, and a release script updates the website's download dialog with the new version and APK size.
